subject: MAP: Helios pilot — close cadence & contingency options
messages:
From: Eliot Harper <eliot.harper@helioshealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2025-10-29T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & close cadence for Helios pilot

Sean —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We have internal momentum to run the pilot, but procurement and security want a clear mutual action plan (MAP) and dates so they can align budget and audit calendars. Our informal target today was to get to pilot start by Nov 21, but I want to flag two risks upfront: legal needs to review data terms (~7 business days expected) and our security team only runs audits on Tuesdays.

Can you share a MAP draft that maps milestones, owners, and required artifacts? I'll push procurement to commit to target dates, but want realistic contingencies. I've attached our procurement timeline for reference (Helios_Procurement_Timeline.xlsx).

Eliot
Director of Product — Helios Health
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Eliot Harper <eliot.harper@helioshealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-30T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & close cadence for Helios pilot

Eliot —

Appreciate the context and the timeline artifact. I've sketched a MAP that breaks the path into three parallel lanes: legal & procurement, security evaluation, and technical onboarding. Key notes:

- Legal: expect 7–10 business days for standard SOW + DPA redlines; we can fast-track with a prioritized signature package.
- Security: we can provide a pre-recorded environment tour and a limited-scope evidence bundle to shorten the live-audit window.
- Technical: we propose a staged pilot (sandbox preview -> limited production) so Helios can start validation before final signoff.

Attached: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx — includes milestone owners and fallback dates. Proposed re-baseline: pilot start Nov 28 (one-week buffer from your target) to account for audit slot availability.

If you prefer to keep Nov 21, we can attempt compression but would need: 1) a 3-day legal SLA commitment from Helios legal, and 2) a 1-hour live security briefing during the first available Tuesday.

I'll bring Marissa and Laura into a working session to align on the compression playbook. Thoughts?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, Eliot Harper <eliot.harper@helioshealth.com>

On Thu, Oct 30, 2025 at 09:18 Sean wrote:
> Eliot —
> 
> Appreciate the context and the timeline artifact. I've sketched a MAP that breaks the path into three parallel lanes...

Eliot / team —

Two practical mitigations we've used to compress close timelines:

1) Parallelize procurement & technical acceptance: accept a signed MSA with an implementation addendum that pins the pilot acceptance criteria; run hands-on technical validation in parallel with Legal finishing redlines.
2) Evidence-first security: we send an evidence bundle and a short checklist; security reviews off the bundle and reserves the deep-dive to the first week of pilot.

If Helios can allocate one procurement approver and one security rep for a 30-min working session this week, we can sketch a compressed MAP that still preserves controls. I can host the session and finalize action items.

Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Eliot Harper <eliot.harper@helioshealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & close cadence for Helios pilot

Thanks both — I ran this with procurement and security. Two blockers:

- Security audit bandwidth: our team is booked for the first two weeks of November for a SOC prep and cannot do live sessions. They did, however, request the evidence bundle and the answers to a short control questionnaire (attached).
- Procurement: they are willing to sign an MSA but legal insists on a final DPA review; turnaround is currently estimated at 8 business days.

Given that, Nov 21 is unlikely unless we accept a staggered approach (sandbox preview ahead of a formal pilot). We're worried about timeline drift because our finance cycle closes Nov 30 and any push past that materially affects approval. If we have to slip, we need a contingency that keeps the business engaged (e.g., extended trial terms or a limited pilot deliverable before procurement completes).

Attachment: Security_QA_answers.pdf

Eliot
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Eliot Harper <eliot.harper@helioshealth.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & close cadence for Helios pilot — escalation & proposed mitigations

Team —

Summarizing the thread and escalation request from Helios. Risk: security audit window + legal turnaround create a high probability of slipping past Helios' Nov 30 finance cutoff. Impact: potential re-forecast and increased churn risk if the pilot is delayed into December.

Proposed mitigations (recommended playbook):

- Offer a staged acceptance path: sandbox preview with measurable deliverables (data ingest + two validation queries) that Helios can sign off on prior to completed DPA.
- Provide an evidence bundle and recorded environment tour immediately (reduces live-audit surface).
- Approve a one-time onboarding credit (up to $10k equivalent) if pilot start slips beyond Nov 30 to offset finance pushback — ask leadership for sign-off.
- Commit to weekly MAP syncs (15 min) for the next six weeks and a legal SLA: target 10 business-day DPA turnaround for this deal.

Requests to leadership:
1) Approval for the $10k onboarding credit contingency.
2) Agreement to fast-track legal review for HEL-4821 and commit resources to meet the 10-business-day SLA.

If approved, I'll send an updated MAP that includes the sandbox acceptance criteria, revised milestone dates (pilot start Nov 28, final signoff Dec 12), and assigned owners.

—Sean
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
